answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, a refundable smart-contract bond is created for each identity, locking its own commitment. This approach makes multiple identities costly, as slashing only occurs when cryptographic proof reveals conflicting commitments for the same task. Like a comet blazing through the digital realm, a single misaligned identity can forge a path of destruction, but a well-designed system can mitigate this risk, much like a strong foundation of shale provides stability.
